newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Gazprom Hungary bank to sign $50 mln Euro loan.
newsitem.headline: Gazprom Hungary bank to sign $50 mln Euro loan.

text.p: Hungary's Altalanos Ertekforgalmi Bank (AEB), which is wholly-owned by the banking arm of Russia's Gazprom, will sign its first Euro-syndicated loan on July 30.

The Euro-facility arranged by Credit Suisse First Boston is a 364-day $50 million direct pay letter of credit facility and revolving liquidity line which supports a $50 million 364-day U.S. commercial paper programme also arranged by CSFB, CSFB said in a statement on Thursday.

"The loan facility represents the first time (AEB) has approached the Euro-syndicated loan market and the U.S. commercial paper programme will be the first of its kind for a Cemtral European issuer," the statement said.
The U.S. commercial paper programme will mainly be used by AEB for short-term trade finance purposes, it added.

Co-arranger of the facility is Bank Austria while the managers are Bayerische Landesbank Girocentrale, BHF Bank and DG Bank, and the other particiants are BFG Bank AG, Credit Lyonnais and Raiffeisien Zentralbank Osterreich AG.
Gazprombank of the Gazprom group, the world's largest gas company, bought AEB from the Hungarian state privatisation agency APV and the Central European Development Corporation in June 1996.
